approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would create an independent anti-corruption body for the Commonwealth, called the Australian National Integrity Commission.
The Commission would have Royal Commission powers to investigate corruption involving federal politicians and the public sector, and could hold public hearings where in the public interest.
The bill limits corruption investigations to conduct within the last ten years and initially excludes federal judges, with a review process for their later inclusion.
Establishes the Australian National Integrity Commission as an independent anti-corruption agency.
Gives the Commission Royal Commission powers to investigate and hold public inquiries into corruption.
Creates a Whistleblower Protection Commissioner within the Commission.
Limits investigations to corrupt conduct occurring in the past ten years.
Excludes federal judges from the Commission's jurisdiction initially, with a review process for their inclusion.
Requires mandatory reporting of corruption by public officials and agency heads.
Federal politicians, the federal public sector, private sector businesses, whistleblowers, and Commonwealth agency heads would be affected.
